## New Investigation Ideas

- **[2026-11-09] The 11-05 AI-capex rout gives a first real test of which of Fred's longs secretly carry AI risk, and the one-day numbers are not the ones the wiki predicted. Only Keller was flagged (10-13). Ero Copper and the QXO preferred fell harder.** On 11-05 (S&P −4.4%, VIX 28, per the PFE paper trade in log.md; SMH about −11% per [[finance/market-sector-performance]]) the three AI puts in [[finance/trading-portfolio]] gained €927 (NBIS −14.9%, PLTR −9.7%, ORCL −6.9%). The long book's losers that day were ERO −8.9%, QXO-PB −5.9%, KLR −5.5%, SFM −5.2% and ZOE −3.8%, while PRX, EDEN and WKL rose. The 10-12 and 10-13 connections in this file named only EOG and KLR as hidden AI-build-out longs. Copper (ERO) and building products (QXO) are plausible AI-power plays too, but nobody has written that down. One day proves little: S&P fell 4.4% overall, and LSE/Euronext close before the US session. **Next step:** pull 60 days of daily closes from Turso for every live long and regress each one on SMH with SPY as a control. The SMH coefficient that is left shows how much of the book moves with the puts' underlyings. That number would show whether the puts are a hedge or are cancelled out by the longs.

[[crypto/crypto-portfolio]]'s 11-07 refresh shows BTC −2.0% and LINK −6.5% since 10-31 and does not mention the election. So one of the rebound catalysts behind Fred's BTC/ETH/LINK holdings has resolved against them. That is worth noting on the crypto pages before the next refresh treats the drawdown as cyclical noise.

## New Cross-Domain Connections

- **[2026-11-08] Lightfin's Shell Heist already acts out a real economics idea, the "vacancy chain": when one crab moves into a bigger shell, its old shell goes to the next crab down, and so on. That gives the Lightfin-skinned Children's Financial Literacy Game a money lesson the show already has characters for, and it doesn't depend on interest.** [[lightfin/ep-305-shell-heist]] teaches that hermit crabs "upgrade shells as they grow", and its plot depends on it. Doug is trying on a new shell when the old one is lost, and his cousin Ernie's motive is that he "wanted Doug's old shell". In real hermit crabs this is a studied behaviour (Ivan Chase's vacancy-chain work): crabs queue by size around an empty shell, then swap down the line, so one new shell can rehouse a whole group. Economists and sociologists use the same model for housing chains and job ladders (Harrison White, *Chains of Opportunity*). The two game ideas logged so far, coral coins (07-19) and the autobattler's capped interest rule (11-06), are both about saving. A shell chain teaches a different lesson that kids can see: trading up, why one purchase frees up something for someone else, and why a missing link (Doug's lost shell) leaves a whole line stuck. [[lightfin/characters]] already has Doug and Ernie. `raw/games/Childrens Financial Literacy Game.md` still has its "sketch a Lightfin-universe version" todo open, and [[games/prototypes]] has no row for it yet. Smallest next step: when that row is written, list "shell-swap chain (Doug and Ernie)" next to coral coins as a candidate mechanic, so it has a Lightfin-native core and not only a reskin.
